knowledge.content: Task constraint: Only modify /app/user.cpp - do not modify any other files in the system
System has two libstdc++ versions: Debug at /usr/local/gcc-custom-debug/ (no optimizations), Release at /usr/local/gcc-custom-release/ (with optimizations). Modified in-house compiler.
Compiler libstdc++ source code location: /build/ directory
Requirement: No memory leaks detected by Valgrind
Problem: Program crashes in RELEASE mode but works in DEBUG mode
File structure at /app/: main.cpp (195 lines), user.cpp (13 lines), user.h. User code is minimal - empty implementations of user_init(), user_cleanup(), and user_main().

main.cpp implements custom heap manager with global operator new/delete overrides. Global pointer g_custom_heap controls whether custom allocator is used. CustomHeapManager allocates 10MB heap upfront, uses bump-pointer allocation (heap_offset), deallocate() is a no-op.

Application lifecycle: init() calls user_init() then creates CustomHeapManager via placement new into malloc'd memory. run() calls user_main() then runs Monte Carlo π estimation. shutdown() explicitly calls CustomHeapManager destructor then frees memory. Destructor also called in ~Application().
Critical bug pattern: CustomHeapManager destructor called twice - once in shutdown() (line 177) and again in ~Application() (line 186 calls shutdown()). This is double-free on heap_memory pointer.
Custom operator new/delete (lines 72-118): Checks g_custom_heap pointer to decide between custom allocator or malloc/free. Four operators defined: new, new[], delete, delete[].

Root cause identified: Double-destruction bug in main.cpp. CustomHeapManager destructor is called twice: (1) explicitly at line 177 in shutdown(), and (2) again at line 186 in ~Application() which calls shutdown(). This causes double-free of heap_memory pointer. The crash only manifests in release mode due to optimization differences.

Fix strategy: Must prevent double-destruction in user.cpp since main.cpp cannot be modified. Need to add guard logic or intervene in the lifecycle to prevent the second destructor call from executing on already-freed memory.

procedural.content: Step 4: Both debug and release builds compiled successfully with their respective commands and library paths. No compilation errors encountered.

Step 5: Confirmed crash behavior - debug version runs successfully (exit 0), release version crashes with exit code -11 (SIGSEGV) after completing all computation. Crash occurs during shutdown/cleanup phase, not during execution. Output is identical until program termination.

Valgrind does not detect the SIGSEGV crash when running the release binary - exits with code 0 and shows 73,728 bytes still reachable but no memory leaks. Direct execution of release binary crashes with exit code -11 (SIGSEGV). This timing/optimization difference suggests the double-free is handled differently under Valgrind's instrumentation vs native execution.

status: Step 9: Agent identified potential root cause - static libstdc++ objects being allocated from custom heap after line 149 but destroyed after heap cleanup. Testing fix strategy: initialize stdlib features in user_init() (line 146) before custom heap is set up, ensuring static objects use regular malloc instead of custom allocator.
